title: AI Conversation Starters for Families
subtitle: 50 questions to open real conversations with your child about AI
subject: Family Conversations
Digital Literacy
summary: A practical card deck of conversation starters organized by topic — from homework and creativity to privacy and jobs. No expertise required. Pick one at dinner and see where it goes.

body.text: You don't need a plan. Pick any question that feels relevant to your family right now and ask it over a meal, in the car, or whenever conversation naturally opens up. These are starting points — follow your child's lead from there. The goal is curiosity, not correction.

items: Have you used an AI tool for a school assignment? What did you use it for?
If an AI helps you write a paper, do you feel like you still learned something?
Does your school have rules about AI? Do they seem fair to you?
Has a teacher talked to you about AI? What did they say?
Have you ever turned in something an AI wrote and felt weird about it?
If AI can answer most test questions, what do you think school is actually for?
Has an AI ever told you something that turned out to be wrong? What happened?
Do you trust AI more or less than a search engine? Why?
When you get an answer from an AI, do you usually check it somewhere else?
What kinds of questions do you think AI is bad at answering?
If an AI sounds very confident, does that make you trust it more?
If you used AI to help make something — a song, a story, an image — is it still yours?
Is there anything creative you'd never want AI's help with? Why?
Have you seen AI-generated art or writing that surprised you — in a good or bad way?
Do you think AI-generated content should be labeled? Why or why not?
What jobs do you think AI will change the most in your lifetime?
Is there anything you're learning now that you think AI will make unnecessary?
What skills do you think will matter more because of AI, not less?
If you could ask the people who build AI systems one question, what would it be?
Do you think AI treats everyone fairly? What makes you think that?
Have you ever felt like an app or website knew too much about you?
When you use a free AI tool, what do you think you're giving up in exchange?
Should AI be allowed to make decisions about things like college admissions or job applications?
